title: Token amount before viewing a used vehicle vs. viewing first, token at the meeting
summary: The recipient enquired on BechoBazaar about a used motorcycle listed in their city. The seller calls back, describes the bike, and says other buyers are interested. In the legitimate case, the seller arranges a viewing and test ride with the registration papers, and says a token can be paid at the viewing against a written receipt if the buyer likes the bike, with the rest at handover. In the fraud case, the seller asks for a token amount by UPI now to "hold" the bike before the buyer has seen it. This differs from `ec_07` (item shipped from another city, full advance) because the vehicle is local and the request is a smaller "token" before an in-person viewing. The word "token" and the same amount range appear in both cases.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: the buyer; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Vehicle: a used 125–150 cc motorcycle, listed at [AMOUNT_27] (₹25,000–₹1,50,000), in [CITY].
Both sellers describe the bike's year, mileage, and condition, and say several people have called.

fraud.label_rationale: The seller asks the buyer to pay a token by UPI before seeing the vehicle or its papers. Paying for an unseen vehicle to a stranger is the core advance-fee pattern in vehicle listings.
fraud.caller_objective: Collect [AMOUNT_26] (then further "charges") with no vehicle to sell.
stable_facts: The seller says they are "out of town this week" but the bike can be "held" for the buyer.
Token is to [UPI_ID_11]; the seller promises to send the RC photo "after the token".
The seller avoids fixing a viewing date.

The seller will show the RC, insurance, and service records and allow a short test ride.
Full payment happens at handover, together with signed transfer forms.

markers.text: Viewing and test ride arranged before any payment
Token only at the viewing, with a written receipt

cooperative.fraud: Says they will send the token now
cooperative.legitimate: Confirms Saturday and asks for the address

clarifying.fraud: Asks why they cannot see the bike first
clarifying.legitimate: Asks whether the insurance is transferable

resistant.fraud: Says they will pay only after seeing the bike
resistant.legitimate: Says they want a mechanic to inspect it first

suspicious.fraud: Asks for the RC photo and a video call before paying anything
suspicious.legitimate: Asks for the RC photo before coming

fraud: buyer pays (cooperative only), after which the seller asks for a "transport" or "paperwork" charge
buyer refuses and seller stops answering
seller lowers the token and buyer declines.
legitimate: seller agrees to a mechanic inspection
seller sends an RC photo with sensitive numbers covered.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud seller may lower the token, add urgency, or send photos. A reduced token is the same mechanism. They must not switch to QR codes, links, or OTPs. The legitimate seller must not ask for any payment before the viewing.

must_preserve: token" and the same amount range in both cases
token by UPI before viewing in _F
may_vary: vehicle type (motorcycle, scooter, small car with a price range adjusted in both)

ambiguities: Token payments are normal in Indian vehicle sales; the word "token" is not evidence. Timing (before vs. after viewing) and route (UPI to a stranger vs. in person with a receipt) decide the label.
Competition from "other buyers" is mentioned in both cases.
A seller who is genuinely out of town is plausible; in this family only the fraud seller is, so absence is a supporting cue, not the label rule.

evidence_references.claim: Police advise avoiding advance payments in classifieds deals and verifying buyers/sellers (CE08)
Financial cyber fraud can be reported on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
